gaps.sentence: ___ problem is that people don't recycle enough.
gaps.explanation: The problem (the one we are discussing); people in general takes no article.
Both 'happiness' and 'money' are general here, so no article for either gap.

gaps.sentence: ___ sales figures for October look promising.
gaps.explanation: 'The sales figures for October' — defined by the for-phrase.

gaps.sentence: He joined ___ army when he was eighteen.
gaps.explanation: Institutions take 'the': the army, the police, the church.

gaps.sentence: ___ Hyde Park is lovely in autumn.
gaps.explanation: Most park names take no article: Hyde Park, Central Park (exception: the Grands Boulevards style names).

gaps.sentence: I saw ___ film last night, and the film was about mountain climbers.
gaps.hint: first mention of one of many
gaps.explanation: First mention of a countable noun takes 'a'; the second mention becomes 'the' (already written out here).

gaps.sentence: She's got ___ few friends in Madrid, so she visits often.
gaps.explanation: 'A few' means some (positive); 'few' alone means hardly any.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.
